feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. What I had to do in the controller: the 0.10 m track raises turn rate per unit PWM difference by about 20 percent, so I cut kp from 0.8 to 0.7 and kept kd at 0.15, ki at 0 and base_speed at 1.5. I kept kd because iteration 3 (80 mm row, kp 0.8, kd 0.15) had steering_oscillation of 0.12 to 0.17, which did not show excess jitter, and no steady offset appeared in any run (RMS 0.019 to 0.033 m). The controller was not changed to fix the 80 mm row, which scored best in iteration 3 (69.18). Decision rules for the next race: if max_error falls to 0.06 m or below on the oval and s-bend while progress stays at or above 0.23 on the oval, keep the 0.10 m track and 80 mm row and try the first requested change. If max_error stays above 0.06 m but steering_oscillation is at or below the iteration 3 level of about 0.12 to 0.17, the peak is not jitter, so the sensor or wheel changes below are the next step. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.17 on the s-bend or slalom, the narrower track has too much gain, so the next step is a controller kp change (for example 0.6), not another geometry change. Progress is the bigger problem: iterations 0 to 3 reached only 0.12 to 0.23 of the course, so the robot is far too slow or leaves the track early, and the speed levers should be considered if max_error is fixed.
requested_changes: If the 0.10 m track with the 80 mm row gives max_error at or below 0.06 m and progress above 0.23, try wheel_radius 0.035 m next, because progress in iterations 0 to 3 (0.12 to 0.23) is far below the full course needed to finish in 3 s, and a larger wheel gives more ground speed at the same PWM.

If steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 3 level (about 0.12 to 0.17) on the s-bend or slalom with the narrower track, try mass 0.7 kg with everything else unchanged, because a slightly heavier body may add yaw damping; this is a hypothesis, since iteration 1 (0.6 kg) lowered oval oscillation to 0.074 but also lowered progress.

If line_loss_events on the slalom stay at 2.0 (iterations 0 and 3) with max_error still above 0.06 m, try sensor_size 0.016 m at the same 80 mm row as a single test, because a larger footprint keeps readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold for longer; iteration 1 changed sensor size with other variables, so its effect is not yet proven.
